name: Sicilian Defense
description: Black's most aggressive and dynamic response to 1.e4, fighting for asymmetrical positions and counter-attacking chances.

variations.name: Najdorf Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6

explanations.e4: White claims the center with the king's pawn.
explanations.c5: Black strikes back asynchronously, defining the Sicilian Defense.
explanations.Nf3: White develops the knight toward the center.
explanations.d6: Black solidifies the center and prepares flexibility.
explanations.d4: White opens central files with an immediate pawn break.
explanations.cxd4: Black trades the flank pawn for White's center pawn.
explanations.Nxd4: White recaptures with the central knight.
explanations.Nf6: Black develops the knight and attacks White's e4-pawn.
explanations.Nc3: White defends e4 with the queen's knight.
explanations.a6: Black plays the Najdorf signature move, preventing b5 checks and controlling b5.

variations.name: Dragon Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6

explanations.g6: Black prepares a fierce dragon setup, fianchettoing the dark-squared bishop.

variations.name: Accelerated Dragon
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 g6

explanations.Nc6: Black develops the queen's knight early.
explanations.g6: Black accelerates the dragon fianchetto, avoiding Maroczy Bind setups.

variations.name: Scheveningen Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e6

explanations.e6: Black creates a flexible, solid pawn structure (Scheveningen setup).

variations.name: Classical Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6

explanations.d4: White trades pawns in the center.
explanations.Nc6: Black develops the knight to its natural classical square.

variations.name: Sveshnikov Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 e5

explanations.e5: Black boldly strikes with e5, accepting a backward d6-pawn for dynamic activity.

variations.name: Kan Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 a6

explanations.a6: Black controls b4 and prevents piece intrusions (Kan Variation).

variations.name: Taimanov Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nc6

explanations.Nc6: Black develops the knight to put immediate pressure on d4.

variations.name: Closed Sicilian
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. g3 g6 4. Bg2 Bg7

explanations.Nc3: White opts for a positional Closed Sicilian setup.
explanations.g3: White prepares to fianchetto the bishop.
explanations.Bg7: Black develops the bishop to the long diagonal.

variations.name: Alapin Variation
variations.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. c3 d5 3. exd5 Qxd5 4. d4 Nf6

explanations.c3: White plays the Alapin, preparing a strong d4 pawn duo.
explanations.d5: Black strikes immediately in the center to challenge White's plan.
explanations.d4: White establishes a firm pawn grip.
explanations.Nf6: Black develops the knight attacking d4.
